headline: Mercedes-Benz Halts New Investment at German Plants
deck: The automaker is reviewing which German sites it can afford after talks over costs failed to produce a solution corridor.
body: Mercedes-Benz has stopped all further investment in its German sites, Michael Schiebe, the production board member, said in an interview published on the company intranet. Schiebe said the decision followed intensive talks that had not produced a “solution corridor” for costs. [E1] [E2]

The interview reported by tagesschau says Mercedes is examining in detail which German sites it can still afford. It says plant closures should be avoided “at all costs” but that the option must now be pursued more concretely. [E3] [E4]

The interview says production-hour costs in Germany can be up to five times those at Eastern European locations; FAZ reported the same comparison. It says new models would be made exclusively outside Germany if no agreement is reached. [E5] [E6] [E7]
